messages.subject: Error with geom_ribbon and scale_x_continuous?
parts:
I'm using geom_ribbon to create a confidence interval and I wanted to
zoom in on the graph. After adding the scale_x_continuous function,
large chunks of the ribbon also got removed.

x=seq(0,1,length=100)
data <- data.frame(x=x, ymin=x-.1, ymax=x+.1)

# Ribbon exists on x-values between 0 and 1
ggplot(data, aes(x=x)) +
geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=ymin, ymax=ymax))

# I expect the ribbon to exist on x-values between 0.6 and 1
# but it only shows up for 0.7 to 0.9... corresponding to the major
grid lines
ggplot(data, aes(x=x)) +
geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=ymin, ymax=ymax)) +
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(.6,1)) +
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(.6,1))

This can easily be worked around by just removing the appropriate rows
of my data.frame, but figured it was worth learning why this isn't a
bug, or making the bug known.

Thanks,

Derek

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: Error with geom_ribbon and scale_x_continuous?
parts:
Derek, that's not a bug. It's a feature, setting the scale limits also removes the data that's not between those limits. If you want to zoom use coord_cartesian, or one of the coord_* functions.

HTH
Luciano

messages.subject: Re: Error with geom_ribbon and scale_x_continuous?
parts:
Got it.

There is a big difference between removing data (what
scale_x_continuous is doing) and then making the graph versus making a
graph and then zooming in (which is what coord_cartesian is doing).

The interaction between the two scales was removing data points I
wasn't expecting and thus, chopping off the ribbon.

Thanks!

Derek
